correctness.rationale: For every m,n>=1, a forbidden rook geodesic is exactly a P4 in the chosen-edge subgraph of K_mn; connected bipartite P4-free graphs are precisely stars. Component EGF is exp(x exp(zy)+y exp(zx)-zxy); disjoint high-degree column stars yield finite sum. Forest component counting proves leading coefficients, with all thin boundaries treated. The attached integer verifier checks 104306 literal vertex subsets across ten small sizes and seven extra large comparisons; finite checking is only corroboration.

General Position Polynomials (2024), full text discusses Cartesian products of paths but does not provide this rook-graph polynomial.
Rather, arXiv:2603.06930, full-text sections on complete multipartite graphs, a distinct product class.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2021 Cartesian-product theorem implies the degree m+n-2 for m,n>=3; that degree is expressly credited. Neither an exact polynomial nor mn distinct maximum subsets follows solely from the maximum-size statement. General-graph structural conditions do not directly supply the enumerator without additional star-forest counting; no broader covering enumeration was located.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The degree statement is a known consequence and not a standalone originality claim. The accepted claim is the exact polynomial for every m,n, its two-sort EGF and full maximal-set multiplicities. These are not logical consequences of the numerical degree alone, nor directly stated by the inspected general structural criteria without the additional enumerative theorem and proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: General-position rook-graph subsets and (3,2)-independent vertex subsets agree here, and via the line-graph construction both are precisely P4-free edge subsets in K_{m,n}. The general characterization supplies a broad necessary and sufficient criterion but does not itself state the two-sort exact polynomial, closed sum, or optimizer count. Equivalent names were searched; no identical counting formula identified.

evidence: Related published exact formulas enumerate general-position sets in generalized windmills, spiders and complete multipartite graphs; not rectangular rook graphs.
The submitted computation reproduces every coefficient independently for ten small boards and by two formulas for seven additional sizes.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No exact tabulation matching the rook-graph polynomials or all-parameter bipartite star-forest EGF was identified. Nonmatching graph polynomials (domination, acyclic-forest, arboricity) do not imply the exact star-component enumeration.

originality.rationale: Compared exact implication against directly relevant 2021 complete-factor Cartesian-product result (degree already known), 2019 broad general-position characterization, the 2024 general-position polynomial paper, 2026 (3,2) independence framework and 2026 formulas for distinct complete multipartite family. No source inspected supplies all coefficients for K_m square K_n or the bipartite star-forest EGF and leading multiplicity; bibliographic priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: An exact bipartite star-forest enumeration or rook-graph general-position polynomial could exist under unsearched terminology.
The 2019 general criterion implies structural aspects, but no inspected explicit all-parameter coefficient formula was located.
Definitive priority and external independent mathematical validation have not been established.

value.rationale: A complete subset-size distribution refines a previously known extremal parameter on a canonical two-parameter graph family and is equivalent to enumerating all labeled spanning star forests of complete bipartite graphs. It offers a uniform bivariate EGF, finite coefficient formula, and exact extremal multiplicities mn, 2^n and boundary counts. This is not merely a fixed small-board calculation or a restatement of the maximum size.
